# Strings, IWTs, and HUDs Pro Tips

Source: [wiki article 5734](../archive/5734.md); edited 2025-04-15.

<a id="wiki-5734-n2"></a>

- A Custom String node is documented as limited to 128 characters, not bytes. Nesting nodes can form longer strings; the former total 511-byte cap is documented as removed.

<a id="wiki-5734-n3"></a>

- Documents maximum 4 icons/textures per string and increased join/startup cost from many strings.

<a id="wiki-5734-n4"></a>

- Leading newline can display a square; prepend a space. Strings are UTF-8.

<a id="wiki-5734-n5"></a>

- Language-dependent censorship can corrupt encoded data: host who last edited/loaded the code determines filtering, replacements become stars. Article recommends nonalphanumeric alphabets for data serialization and notes numeric display can also be affected.

<a id="wiki-5734-n6"></a>

- Localized String is described as legacy by the source author; this is advice, not an engine prohibition. Account for the documented font and translation differences between client languages.

<a id="wiki-5734-n7"></a>

- Font mapping: HUD header Industry Black, Big Message Big Noodle, usual text Config, fallback/progress-bar IWT Blizzard Global. A missing glyph changes the entire string to fallback; a line-separator character can force Blizzard Global.

<a id="wiki-5734-n8"></a>

- Only Blizzard Global is documented consistent across languages; manual alignment with other fonts can break in Asian language clients.

<a id="wiki-5734-n9"></a>

- HUD layer order is left below right below top; left/right share vertical start, top differs. Group centering depends on all HUDs, spaces/newlines can shift alignment and displace objective/killfeed UI.

<a id="wiki-5734-n10"></a>

- Right HUD negative sort order keeps it above killfeed; otherwise killfeed shifts it down. Large trailing-space padding can force grouping/alignment, but other HUDs in that group are affected.

<a id="wiki-5734-n11"></a>

- HUD header direct Null or empty string hides it; Null stored in a variable instead displays 0. Zero-width spaces in text/subheader can preserve layout while header visibility changes.

<a id="wiki-5734-n12"></a>

- IWT/progress-bar IWT documented combined cap 128; size decreases slightly with distance; progress-bar text is 1.25 times ordinary IWT and has a thinner outline with Blizzard Global only.

<a id="wiki-5734-n13"></a>

- For complex IWT overlays, shared anchor plus matched line counts avoids difficult geometric alignment. Block is horizontally centered, individual lines left-aligned; ordinary IWT shifts downward with additional lines, while progress-bar text bottom remains anchored.

<a id="wiki-5734-n14"></a>

- OW2 removes trailing spaces from IWT lines; a terminal zero-width space preserves intended padding. Documented coordinate box is +/-2000 per axis, playable area +/-1000; distant placement reduces sway but must stay within bounds.

<a id="wiki-5734-n16"></a>

- String-based vector-data encoding can reduce element count; parsing cost and censorship must be considered. Article's separator example is pedagogical and intentionally followed by a safer-alphabet caveat.
